articles.title: A retired US nurse lost more than $200,000 to a scammer posing as a federal agent; then the IRS sent her an $80,000 tax bill and she had to sell her home
articles.summary: US News: A retired nurse, Susan Bivins, was tricked into sending more than $200,000 to a scammer who pretended to be a federal agent. Bivins said she reported .
articles.body: A retired nurse, Susan Bivins, was tricked into sending more than $200,000 to a scammer who pretended to be a federal agent. Bivins said she reported the fraud to the FBI and local police, but did not receive the help she had hoped for. The financial damage became even worse when she later received a tax bill from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).The IRS said she owed $80,000 in taxes on money she had withdrawn from her retirement accounts and then lost to the scammer. With no way to cover the bill, Bivins sold her home and moved into a small one-bedroom apartment. “I wanted to drive off a cliff,” she said as quoted by Washington Post. “I didn’t know how I was going to live.”Bivins is among dozens of scam victims interviewed by news agency Associated Press and Frontline as part of an investigation into the growing impact of online fraud in the US. The victims came from different age groups and financial backgrounds. They felt confused and abandoned after losing their money.Victims can lose moreThe investigation found that losing money to a scam can be only the beginning of a victim’s financial problems. Some victims were left with bank fees, loan repayments and tax bills after scammers took their money.US consumers reported a record $15.9 billion in scam losses to the Federal Trade Commission last year. That was a 25% increase from 2024. However, the actual losses could be much higher because many victims do not report scams due to embarrassment or shame. The FTC estimated actual losses in 2024 to be close to $200 billion in the US.The growth of artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency has also made scams more sophisticated. AI can help scammers operate on a much larger scale, while cryptocurrency can make it difficult to identify who ultimately controls stolen funds.A poll by the Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research found that 98% of Americans believed they had been targeted by scammers. Three in 10 said they had personally lost money or information to a scam.AP and FRONTLINE interviewed 58 people in the US who lost money to cyber scams. Their losses ranged from several thousand dollars to $4 million. The victims included doctors, IT professionals, academics and people struggling to make ends meet.Tax rules add to burdenFor some victims, the financial impact continues even after the scam has ended. The IRS can require people to pay taxes on money withdrawn from tax-deferred retirement accounts, even when that money is later stolen. Tax-deferred accounts are retirement accounts where taxes on certain income are generally delayed until money is withdrawn.Before 2018, victims of theft or fraud could sometimes deduct their losses from taxable income. But a provision in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act removed tax breaks for personal losses from many common scams. That provision was made permanent in 2025. This means victims can be left paying taxes on money that they no longer have. That was what happened to Bivins.After losing more than $200,000 to the scammer posing as a federal agent, she was faced with an $80,000 IRS bill. She sold her home to deal with the financial pressure and now lives in a smaller apartment. She is still paying off the tax bill by selling handmade quilts.A bill currently before Congress, called the Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act, would bring back an allowance for victims to deduct losses from certain scams. Kathy Stokes, AARP’s fraud prevention lead, said victims should not be left with financial obligations created by crimes against them. “Essentially they’re being revictimized by the US government,” Stokes said.Struggle to recover moneyRecovering stolen money can be difficult even when victims report the crime quickly. Victims told AP and FRONTLINE that they often faced pressure from banks and lenders after the fraud. Some said their accounts were frozen or closed, while others were asked to repay loans or cover legal costs.Under current US law, banks are generally not required to reimburse customers when the customers themselves authorised the transactions after being tricked. Banks are more likely to be responsible when money is taken without the customer's authorisation.Cryptocurrency can make recovery even harder. Unlike bank deposits, crypto assets are not backed by federal insurance. Transfers can also make it harder to identify the people involved, while many cryptocurrency exchanges operate across borders.Brian Glick, who lost $575,000, contacted the FBI, an elder abuse hotline, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the New York State Attorney General’s office. He also submitted complaints and collected thousands of screenshots.The FBI contacted cryptocurrency company Tether in an attempt to freeze funds connected to Glick’s case. Tether said the funds had already been moved and mixed with other money by the time it was contacted.Congress is considering more than a dozen bills related to scams. Proposals include creating a central website for reporting scams and requiring disclosures for deepfakes and other AI-generated audio and video.The Justice Department has also created a Scam Center Strike Force aimed at targeting criminal networks behind scams and seizing stolen funds. However, victims say these measures have not kept pace with the scale of the problem.The FBI receives nearly 3,000 internet crime complaints a day on average through its IC3 reporting system. Former FBI unit chief Donna Gregory said the agency can investigate only about 10% to 12% of the cases reported through IC3.r.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: US President Donald Trump is considering declaring war on Iran, even as the Pentagon extends troop deployments in West Asia. According to a latest report by the Wall Street Journal, Trump has been mulling over whether to discontinue the war that has extended over seven months now. The discussions come against the backdrop of the Pentagon upping its military presence in the West Asia region.The development came as the US and Iran exchanged new attacks on Tuesday, with the latest escalation raising questions over whether Washington is preparing to wind down the conflict or keep military options open.The US central command (CENTCOM) said on Wednesday that American forces had struck multiple sites inside Iran. Tehran responded with attacks on US-linked facilities across the Gulf. Iranian officials said the latest US strikes killed 18 people and wounded 142 others.Amid the fighting, the US also escorted 40 commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, two US officials told CNN. It was the largest number of ships protected in a single operation since the war began, according to the officials.US forces also struck nearly 60 Iranian military sites around the Strait of Hormuz. The targets included air defence systems, radar installations, maritime infrastructure, mine-laying facilities and communications networks.Despite the continued military action, Trump has discussed with senior aides “whether to declare the Iran war over", according to the WSJ report. The president privately favours such a move, particularly as the US mid-term elections approach and the conflict pushes up energy prices.Trump believes Iran will eventually dismantle its nuclear programme under mounting economic pressure. His administration last week launched Operation Economic Outcast, aimed at weakening Tehran's main economic lifelines.The operation targets key sectors including oil, shipping, aviation and digital assets.However, the Pentagon appears to be preparing for the possibility that the conflict will continue.US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is quietly extending troop deployments in West Asia, the Wall Street Journal reported. The move is “in a sign that the conflict could drag well into next year".The extensions are intended to preserve the president's military choices while the conflict remains unresolved. The decision would give Trump “options in the war", according to people familiar with the matter cited by the newspaper.The contrasting moves highlight the uncertainty surrounding the US strategy. articles.title: A $6.9 billion Ohio data-centre project would cover about 300 acres; after resident backlash, Grove City imposed a one-year moratorium, and a ballot fight is now underway
articles.summary: US News: In Ohio's Grove City, a proposed charter amendment has sparked a fight that doesn't seem to end. Residents and leaders are clashing on two sides, with.
articles.body: In Ohio's Grove City, a proposed charter amendment has sparked a fight that doesn't seem to end. Residents and leaders are clashing on two sides, with one saying the amendment would protect the city and others saying it would destroy its economic prospects. What highlights the conflict is that it is a microcosm of a nationwide pushback against data centres and the region makes one of the most extreme local attempts to stop them, as per a report by Axios.The pushback is on a planned 300-acre project valued at approximately $6.9 billion. It would be a high-density computing/data-centre campus, designed to provide infrastructure for the rapidly expanding AI and cloud-computing industry. According to the developers, the site was deliberately selected since it exists next to a 345-kilovolt electrical substation, which they say makes the location suitable for a power-intensive facility. The project has raised concerns about electricity demand, water use, noise, backup generators, traffic, environmental impacts, and the long-term character of Grove City.The backlash was so intense that the city council enacted a one-year moratorium on all data centre projects, including the $6.9 billion planned campus. The opposition group known as Protect Grove City did not stop at the moratorium. They went on to draft a charter amendment that aims to block data centres and other large development projects unless voters approve them individually. They managed to collect more than 2,000 signatures, enough to force city council to add the proposed amendment to the November ballot.The amendment doesn't just limit data centres. If passed, any Grove City development that occupies 50 or more acres, uses 20 megawatts of power or consumes 500,000 gallons of water a day would be subjected to a referendum. It would also require the developer to pay for related ballot costs.On the other side, some city and regional economic development leaders claim the amendment's effects would be devastating. "It would literally kill the city," said Council President Ted Berry to Axios. "This is not a data centre amendment," says former U.S. Rep. and current Ohio Chamber of Commerce CEO Steve Stivers. "It's a development amendment, and it basically says, 'We don't want to grow.'"Interestingly, this is a risk that the opposition group is willing to deal with as they say their initiative is an effort to "give people a voice." Jen Belt, one of the group's leaders, said they feel the city leaders are no longer representing them. "What we're seeing around the country is that our interests are not being considered. You're not hearing us."At a special meeting on Thursday, the day before the deadline for council to put it on the ballot, the group will ask council to replace the original amendment with a "compromise" version that replaces the 50 acres with 750,000 square feet of floor area and removes requirements for existing companies. Protect Grove City would withdraw the previous amendment if council sent the new one to the ballot.However, the new version drafted this week had not undergone public vetting yet. Council is unlikely to adopt it instead of the amendment for which the petitioners collected signatures. "It's almost like a blackmailing technique," Berry said.Belt added the group was "willing to come to the table" in good faith, which isn't blackmail.Berry claimed the issue "fails miserably" in his own polling and seems ready to let it go to the ballot as written. "Obviously, the tide has turned, and they don't have the support to get it passed," he said."Whichever version goes on the ballot, we'll be campaigning for the passage of that this November," Belt said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘6ft by 8ft cell, brown drinking water’: What Imran Khan’s jail cell is like
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan is being held in what has been described as harsh conditions at Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail, with reports alleg.
articles.body: Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan is being held in what has been described as harsh conditions at Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail, with reports alleging prolonged isolation, limited access to reading material and restrictions on contact with his family.According to a report by The Times UK, Khan is being kept in a 6ft by 8ft cell typically used for prisoners on death row. The report said the 73-year-old has no reading material apart from the Quran and is being provided “soiled brown water” to drink.His sons, Sulaiman and Kasim Khan, have reportedly been unable to meet their father in person since 2022 and have at times been prevented from speaking to him by telephone for months. They have described his living conditions as inhumane “torture tactics”.The report said visitors have been barred and Khan has been confined to his cell for as much as 23 hours a day.The reported restrictions have also become the subject of repeated legal challenges by Khan’s family.His sister Uzma Khan filed a fresh contempt petition in the Supreme Court on Wednesday, alleging that authorities have failed to comply with an August 18 order concerning Khan’s access to his family.According to The Express Tribune, the petition names Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Adiala Jail Superintendent Sajid Baig, Punjab Inspector General of Prisons Mian Salik Jalal and other senior officials as respondents.The August 18 order had directed authorities to facilitate virtual communication between Khan and his sons and allow his sisters to meet him weekly. However, Uzma said she was denied a scheduled visit on Tuesday, while telephone communication between Khan and his sons has remained restricted since March.The petition also alleges that authorities failed to establish the infrastructure required for bi-weekly telephone calls with Sulaiman and Kasim.The latest dispute follows an earlier contempt petition over the alleged non-compliance with the Supreme Court’s direction to transfer Khan to Shifa International Hospital for medical evaluation. He was instead taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) on August 21 before being returned to Adiala Jail after doctors declared him “medically fit”. Authorities have cited security concerns for the decision.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: For 35 years, Dolly Parton’s Dollywood protected bald eagles; after a storm damaged their sanctuary, the birds are moving to a new 50-acre campus
articles.summary: Rest of World News: For 35 years, bald eagles had a special place at Dollywood, where the American Eagle Foundation’s Eagle Mountain Sanctuary introduced generations of v.
articles.body: For 35 years, bald eagles had a special place at Dollywood, where the American Eagle Foundation’s Eagle Mountain Sanctuary introduced generations of visitors to one of America’s most recognisable birds. The long-running Dollywood partnership, associated with Dolly Parton’s Tennessee theme park, combined wildlife education with hands-on conservation work and helped bring the story of bald eagle recovery to millions of people. Now, the sanctuary’s future has changed after a storm damaged the facility in 2026. The non-releasable bald eagles that lived there are being permanently relocated to the American Eagle Foundation’s 50-acre conservation and education campus in Kodak, Tennessee. According to the foundation’s August 2026 update, the move marks the end of an important chapter at Dollywood, but not the end of the conservation partnership. The birds will continue receiving care while Dollywood and the foundation maintain their shared commitment to educating visitors about bald eagles and other birds of prey.Dollywood’s 35-year partnership helped protect bald eaglesThe partnership between Dollywood and the American Eagle Foundation began in 1991, creating a conservation relationship that would continue for more than three decades. Through Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, visitors could see bald eagles and learn about the threats that had once placed the species under serious pressure. The American Eagle Foundation says its work during this period included the successful release of more than 400 bald eagles into the wild. Its conservation efforts contributed to a much broader recovery that eventually saw the bald eagle removed from the US list of endangered and threatened species in 2007. In its August 2026 update, the foundation described the Dollywood relationship as an important part of its educational mission. The partnership allowed conservation messages to reach millions of people who might otherwise never encounter rescued or non-releasable birds.A storm damaged the bald eagle sanctuary at DollywoodThe future of Eagle Mountain Sanctuary changed after a storm damaged the facility in 2026. Rather than rebuilding the sanctuary as it had previously operated, the American Eagle Foundation and Dollywood chose to move the non-releasable bald eagles permanently to the foundation’s larger 50-acre conservation campus in Kodak. The American Eagle Foundation explained that the birds had already been receiving care at the campus following the damage. The relocation provides a new long-term home while allowing the organisation to bring more of its conservation, education and bird-care work together. Dollywood’s announcement also presented the move as a transition rather than an end to the relationship. While the sanctuary itself will no longer house the eagles, the birds’ story and the lessons surrounding their protection will continue through the foundation’s wider educational programmes.The 50-acre conservation campus will become the eagles’ new homeThe American Eagle Foundation’s 50-acre campus in Kodak provides considerably more space for its conservation and educational work. The organisation opened its current headquarters and educational campus in 2023 as a base for its mission of protecting birds of prey, caring for non-releasable animals and teaching the public about wildlife. Moving the bald eagles there gives the birds a permanent home while placing them within a broader conservation setting. According to the foundation, the campus will allow it to build on the legacy created through Eagle Mountain Sanctuary and expand its work in the years ahead. The relocation is therefore more than a response to storm damage. It represents a shift towards a larger conservation operation, where the care of rescued birds, public education and wildlife protection can be developed together on one dedicated site.Dollywood will continue its bald eagle conservation partnershipAlthough the bald eagles are leaving Eagle Mountain Sanctuary, the conservation partnership between Dollywood and the American Eagle Foundation is continuing. According to Dollywood’s announcement, the foundation will maintain its presence at the park through the Birds of Prey programme at the Wings of America Theater. Visitors will still have opportunities to encounter bald eagles and other raptors while learning about their biology, behaviour and conservation. Dollywood has described the 35-year relationship as an important way of helping guests develop a deeper appreciation for birds of prey and the natural world. The move therefore changes where the birds are housed without removing the educational connection between Dollywood and the American Eagle Foundation. The partnership’s next chapter will continue focusing on conservation awareness, ensuring that the legacy of Eagle Mountain Sanctuary remains part of the park’s wildlife story.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Provincetown’s most expensive condo sold for $5M just two weeks after another condo set a $3.9M record; the unit found a buyer in only five days
articles.summary: News News: Picture this: You live in Provincetown, one of America's most desirable residential areas, and watch a condo in your neighbourhood sell for a record $.
articles.body: Picture this: You live in Provincetown, one of America's most desirable residential areas, and watch a condo in your neighbourhood sell for a record $3.9 million. You joined the celebrations, shook hands with the new neighbour. But then, nearly two weeks later, the condo next door sells for an even more staggering $5 million, making it the most expensive purchase in the area.That’s exactly what happened in Provincetown recently, when the neighbourhood's escalating luxury game reached a fever pitch. Two stunning condos on the same bucolic West End street, separated by mere feet, shattered records in just fourteen days, with the second deal obliterating the first by over a million bucks! The $5 million condo was a three-bedroom contemporary home designed as a personal retreat.Both properties were developed by local restaurateur Victor DePoalo, who understood the demand for modern homes in a town known for its Victorian-style houses. The condos were listed by agent Thomas Andrews of Gibson Sotheby's International Realty.What the $5 million condo hasThe three-bedroom residence at 170 Bradford Street was sold for $5 million on September 1, according to Realtor.com. Victor DePoalo built the condo for himself in 2019 and has lived in it until now. This sale set a new record in the town at the tip of Cape Cod, marking the highest price ever paid for a condo, Andrews told the WSJ. “The numbers have gone crazy,” the developer told the outlet.This 2,725-square-foot unit is one of five he built on the Bradford Street Extension, which runs parallel to Commercial Street, the town’s main street. The condo has three bedrooms and 4.5 bathrooms spread across three floors. The contemporary home has all the amenities that would be on a resort’s checklist. Think a saltwater gunite pool, pocket doors for flexible living, top-of-the-line appliances and a fireplace. “These two are more contemporary styles,” Andrews told Realtor.com. The high-priced contemporary homes are not a coincidence, especially in a neighbourhood where preservation has a lot of meaning. This resort-like lifestyle is thoughtfully curated and reflects how the buyers would prefer to live.The open kitchen and living area is designed for gathering, while an office nook tucked behind those signature pocket doors is ideal for WFH scenes, along with entertaining purposes. The primary suite on the third floor, with vaulted ceilings and a double vanity, is every luxury one would hope for in a $5 million condo. The secondary bedrooms also live up to the master: high ceilings, expansive windows and en suite options. This condo is put together with a lot of thought, even down to the landscaping that maintains privacy while keeping residents steps from Provincetown's best neighbourhoods. The condo is within walking distance of the town’s best highlights, including the Chelsea Earnest Memorial Playground, a project supported by designer Marc Jacobs.What’s more striking is that the $5 million condo hit the market on a Friday and went under contract by Tuesday. Five days, that’s all it took. The previous record-breaking $3.9 million condo at 168 Bradford Street was sold just two weeks prior. It moved even faster: the deal was closed in a single day!Growing demand for Provincetown propertiesProvincetown sits at the tip of Cape Cod. The location sounds romantic, but there is no space left to expand. Despite this, the demand is only surging, with no signs of slowing down.“The housing stock is therefore relatively fixed, and any new supply has to come from redevelopment or small-scale infill, both of which tend to be expensive and difficult to pull off,” Hannah Jones, senior economist at Realtor.com, explained. But the flourishing creative community and the picturesque views are only making it more desirable.For instance, DePoalo sold one of the five units for $1.8 million when he finished it in 2019. It was later resold in August for $3.9 million. That's not all. Earlier this month, a tiny cottage under 800 square feet was listed for $1.5 million, which means nearly $1,897 per square foot, and it is as absurd as it sounds.“This type of neighbourhood runs very, very tight and is very difficult to get into. Being engaged in the community, on multiple levels, is super important,” Andrews said. He also thinks newcomers should seek the help of an agent to fit in. “It’s highly, highly important to use an agent that’s very well connected with the community on a local level.”Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Indian-origin British Airways manager convicted of sexually assaulting colleague at his home
articles.summary: US News: A British Airways manager of Indian origin, Amardip Dhariwal, has been convicted of sexually assaulting a colleague in Berkshire. The case sheds light on workplace safety and misconduct.
articles.body: An Indian-origin British Airways cabin crew manager has been convicted of sexually assaulting a female colleague at his home in Berkshire after she woke to find him touching her without her consent.Amardip “Amo” Dhariwal, 55, was found guilty of one count of sexual assault by penetration following a nine-day trial at Reading Crown Court.The incident took place at Dhariwal’s home in Bracknell in May 2022 after he and the woman had spent the evening socialising. She woke during the night to find Dhariwal touching her, according to Thames Valley Police.The woman pretended to remain asleep because she was afraid of how he might react if she confronted him. After the assault ended, she left the property, contacted a friend and later reported the incident to police.Dhariwal, who is from Southall, worked for British Airways as an in-flight cabin crew lead.He has been released on strict conditional court bail and will return to Reading Crown Court for sentencing on October 29.Dhariwal had also faced two rape allegations involving two other women in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur. Those charges were dropped because the Crown Prosecution Service lacked jurisdiction to prosecute the alleged offences.Evidence from the two women was nevertheless heard during the trial as bad character evidence against Dhariwal.Detective Constable Clare Hickman of Thames Valley Police praised all three women for their involvement in the case.She commended the main victim for coming forward and continuing to participate in the investigation and court proceedings, while also recognising the other two women for providing evidence.“All three women have shown remarkable resilience, courage and dignity throughout,” Hickman said.Dhariwal will remain on bail until his sentencing hearing.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Dealer kept car for years, failed to transfer ownership; commission orders Rs 2.57 lakh payout
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: The West Bengal state consumer commission has upheld an order directing a car dealer to pay Rs 2.57 lakh to a customer after the dealer fai.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The West Bengal state consumer commission has upheld an order directing a car dealer to pay Rs 2.57 lakh to a customer after the dealer failed to transfer ownership of a second-hand car and kept the vehicle at its workshop for years after an accident. The commission also upheld 10 percent annual interest, Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 towards legal expenses. The order was passed on September 2, 2026.Why did the customer approach the commission?According to the commission order, the customer booked a pre-owned Maruti SX4 on March 10, 2016, under the dealer’s “true value” scheme for Rs 3.69 lakh. He paid Rs 5,000 as booking advance and gave his father’s Maruti Omni, valued at Rs 1.30 lakh, in exchange. He paid the remaining Rs 2.39 lakh to the dealer.The customer also paid Rs 13,000 for administrative and other charges for transferring the car’s ownership and registration. The dealer assured him that the transfer would be completed within six months. The car was delivered on April 5, 2016.Six days later, on April 11, the car met with an accident and was taken to the dealer’s workshop. The dealer issued a repair estimate of Rs 53,780 but did not repair the vehicle. The car remained at the workshop.The customer later sent a legal notice to the dealer. He also faced a problem when the RTO asked him to produce the car for inspection because the vehicle was still inside the dealer’s workshop. He then approached the consumer commission.The dealer argued that the customer was not a consumer, that the complaint was filed late and that ONGC, the earlier registered owner, and the insurance company should also have been made parties. It also said the repairs could not be carried out because the customer had not paid the repair charges.The customer said he had given the dealer all the documents available with him after the accident. He also relied on the delivery note, which stated that the dealer had agreed to take responsibility for helping complete the ownership transfer.Why did the commission rule against the car dealer?The bench of member Rajes Guha Ray and member Santanu Saha found that the dealer had taken Rs 13,000 specifically for transferring the car’s ownership but failed to complete the process within the promised six months. It noted that the dealer did not submit the required papers to the RTO until October 27, 2016.“It is an undisputed fact that the appellant collected Rs.13,000/- specifically to effect the change of ownership and name transfer. The delivery note explicitly bound the Appellant to full responsibility for this transfer. The car was delivered on April 5, 2016, with a clear verbal promise to complete the process within six months,” the bench said.The dealer claimed that the transfer was delayed because the customer failed to produce the car for an RTO inspection. The commission rejected this argument because the car had already been lying inside the dealer’s workshop since the accident.“The appellant argues that the transfer got stalled because the Complainant failed to produce the car for inspection on November 8, 2016. However, this argument is logically flawed. The car had been lying inside the Appellant's workshop since the accident on April 11, 2016, and hence, the Appellant held physical custody of the vehicle. Expecting the complainant to produce a vehicle lying inside the appellant's own garage is absurd,” the commission held.On the repairs, the commission said the dealer could not necessarily be forced to carry out extensive repairs without payment. However, it said the dealer could not keep the customer’s vehicle indefinitely.“However, the deficiency of the Appellant lies in its subsequent conduct. Even if repairs were stalled due to financial and documentation disputes, the Appellant had no legal right to hold the consumer's vehicle in perpetuity, allowing it to deteriorate for years while using the documentation deadlock as a shield,” the commission further noted.The commission dismissed the dealer’s appeal and upheld the district commission’s order directing it to pay Rs 2.57 lakh with 10 percent annual interest, along with Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 legal expenses.The dealer has been directed to pay the entire amount within 45 days. Once the payment is made, it can take possession of the damaged vehicle, which remains at its workshop, as salvage.

articles.title: Feminist activist and Ms Magazine co-founder Gloria Steinem dies at 92
articles.summary: US News: Gloria Steinem, the celebrated author, journalist and activist who became one of the most prominent voices of the US women’s movement and a fierce adv.
articles.body: Gloria Steinem, the celebrated author, journalist and activist who became one of the most prominent voices of the US women’s movement and a fierce advocate for gender equality, has died at the age of 92.Steinem died Wednesday at her home in New York City, according to posts on her and her foundation’s social media accounts.A co-founder of Ms Magazine, Steinem became one of the most recognisable figures of the feminist movement. With her trademark streaked hair, large aviator glasses and distinctive style, she spent decades travelling across the US and abroad, speaking at college campuses, community centres, rallies and marches.Steinem began her career as a journalist. In 1963, she went undercover to report on working conditions at Hugh Hefner’s Playboy Club, an assignment she later said she regretted.Her career took a decisive turn after attending a 1969 meeting where women spoke openly about abortion rights.“That speak-out was the beginning of activism for me,” Steinem told the Associated Press in 2022 while reflecting on the reversal of Roe v Wade. “Either our control over our own bodies is equal, regardless of sex or race, or we’re not living in a democracy.”Steinem had undergone a secret illegal abortion at the age of 22, an experience that later shaped her views on reproductive rights.Although she became a leading public speaker, Steinem said she had initially been deeply afraid of speaking in public. She told the AP in 2015 that she would have preferred to remain a writer if editors had been willing to publish more of her work on the women’s movement.“So I ended up going out and speaking, which was my nightmare,” she said. “I mean, I was terrified. But I’m grateful, even though I still get scared even now.”Steinem remained active well into her 80s, travelling around the world and campaigning on issues ranging from female genital mutilation to Korean reconciliation. Gender equality, however, remained central to her work.Her public presence continued for decades. At 83, she attended her first fashion show, sitting in the front row as a guest of designer Prabal Gurung.At 85, she led a women’s “talking circle” at an off-Broadway play about her life, where audience members shared personal experiences of discrimination and thanked her for her work.In 2020, her life was portrayed in “The Glorias, A Life on The Road”, based on her 2015 memoir and starring Julianne Moore.Steinem remained involved in advocacy and writing in her later years. At 91, she collaborated with Liberian peace activist and Nobel laureate Leymah Gbowee on a picture book aimed at inspiring young people to create change.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Walt Disney built a 2,615-foot railroad in his backyard in 1950; when his house was demolished decades later, one tiny barn was saved and moved
articles.summary: US News: For a few years in the 1950s, Walt Disney had an unusual feature in his Holmby Hills backyard: a working miniature railway stretching for more than ha.
articles.body: For a few years in the 1950s, Walt Disney had an unusual feature in his Holmby Hills backyard: a working miniature railway stretching for more than half a mile. The Carolwood Pacific Railroad ran for 2,615 feet around the property, crossing a trestle, disappearing into a tunnel and passing beneath his wife’s flower bed. Beside the tracks stood a small barn where Disney could operate switches, work on his trains and spend time away from the demands of his growing studio. The railway disappeared after the family’s home was sold and the property was redeveloped. The barn faced the same fate, but it was saved before the old structures were demolished. Dismantled, stored and eventually moved to Griffith Park, the building survives today as a tangible remnant of Disney’s private railroad and a small piece of the setting where he spent time working on ideas.Walt Disney built the Carolwood Pacific Railroad in his backyardDisney began building the Carolwood Pacific Railroad in 1950, naming it after Carolwood Drive, the Holmby Hills street where his family lived. The project gave him a chance to indulge a long-standing interest in railways on a much larger scale than a model train running around a table.According to The Carolwood Foundation, the first train travelled the line on May 7, 1950. By then, Disney had created about 2,615 feet of track around the grounds. The railway included a 46-foot trestle and a 90-foot tunnel, the latter running beneath an area occupied by his wife’s flower bed.Disney could use it to monitor the railway and control its track switches remotely, while the building also gave him somewhere to repair and work on his trains.The barn became a place where railway work could sit alongside the other projects occupying his attention, with friends also using it as somewhere to gather. Its later history would give the otherwise modest building an importance separate from the railroad itself.The barn remained on the property after Disney's house was eventually sold. That became significant when the new owners discovered serious problems with the existing structures, including structural concerns and asbestos. Plans to retain the original house could not go ahead, and the buildings were demolished before a new residence was constructed.Diane Disney Miller found a way to save Disney’s railroad barnThe barn might have disappeared with the rest of the property had Disney’s daughter, Diane Disney Miller, not recognised that it could be preserved separately.Before the sale process was complete, Miller contacted Michael and Sharon Broggie, who had founded the Carolwood Society and were familiar with the history of Disney’s backyard railway. The question was no longer whether the barn could remain where it stood, but whether it could be carefully taken apart and given another home.A contractor, Bill Abel, was brought in to dismantle the structure. The pieces were stored while arrangements were worked out for its eventual relocation. It took an agreement involving the City of Los Angeles and the Los Angeles Live Steamers Museum to establish where the barn could be reconstructed.The Carolwood barn reopened inside a Griffith Park railwayReportedly, the solution was Griffith Park, where the barn was eventually opened to the public on July 19, 1999. It was placed within the Los Angeles Live Steamers Museum’s 1/8-scale railway, matching the scale Disney had used for his own line.The setting is very different from the Holmby Hills backyard, but the railway connection remains. Instead of sitting beside the original house and garden, the barn now occupies a landscaped section of Griffith Park surrounded by the miniature railway.What remains insideThe barn is a relatively small building, but its contents help explain how Disney used it. Items connected with his railroading are displayed there, alongside material relating to the history of the railroad and Disneyland.This was where Disney worked on his trains and spent time thinking through ideas away from the main activity of his professional life. The Carolwood Society describes the barn as having a connection to the early thinking behind what would later become known as Imagineering.The railroad itself is long gone from the Holmby Hills property. The barn is the surviving physical link.The Carolwood barn remains open to visitors in Griffith ParkToday, visitors can see the preserved barn at the Los Angeles Live Steamers Museum on the third Sunday of each month. It is open from 11am to 3pm, with free admission and free parking. Donations are accepted by the museum.The original Carolwood Pacific Railroad no longer winds through Disney’s former backyard. Its trestle, tunnel and 2,615-foot course belonged to a particular place and period of his life. The small barn had a different fate.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Thursday alleged that the appointment of a CEO for the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust marked the beginning of the “corporatisation” of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya.The temple trust, which manages the Ram temple, on Wednesday appointed retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as its first CEO and former treasurer Govind Dev Giri as its new general secretary. This means corporatisation of the temple has taken place. When there is business, there is CEO, managing director, directors.”On Wednesday, the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust selected Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as the first Chief Executive Officer of the Ram temple in Ayodhya.Speaking to TOI, Mishra said, “I came to know about my appointment via news, I’m yet to receive official communication from trust.”The decorated former Indian Air Force commander retired in April 2026 and will now oversee the temple Trust’s expanding administrative responsibilities. However, the standard operating procedure for the appointment and functioning of the CEO has not yet been finalised, said Govind Dev Giri, general secretary of the Trust.Mishra was the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force’s Western Air Command when Operation Sindoor was launched on May 7, 2025, in response to the Pahalgam terror attack.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Homeowner discovers 18.5 kg Viking silver hoard in Denmark after garden fork strikes buried treasure while digging for a new terrace
articles.summary: Europe News: A few hours of garden work in Rebild, Denmark, turned into an extraordinary archaeological discovery when a homeowner uncovered what is now the countr.
articles.body: A few hours of garden work in Rebild, Denmark, turned into an extraordinary archaeological discovery when a homeowner uncovered what is now the country’s largest known Viking Age silver hoard. It was unexpectedly found while the owner was removing stubborn grass, stones and gravel to prepare the ground for a new tiled terrace. After about half an hour of digging, a garden fork struck something that made an unusual sound. What first appeared to be old iron, wire and pottery fragments soon revealed something far more valuable. The homeowner began pulling metal objects from the soil by hand and realised they were jewellery, coins and silver bars. As per North Jutland Museums, the hoard contains around 700 objects and fragments with a combined weight of 18.5 kilograms. It is almost three times heavier than Denmark’s previously largest known Viking silver hoard.What treasures were found in Denmark’s largest Viking silver hoardThe newly discovered hoard contains around 700 objects and fragments weighing a total of 18.5 kilograms. It includes numerous silver bars, bracelets, 47 complete coins and coin fragments, a small Thor’s hammer and various pieces of cut silver objects. About 320 objects weighing 6.4 kilograms were still inside the original clay vessel when the discovery was made. The remaining objects were scattered in the surrounding soil. It is almost three times larger than the Terslev hoard, previously considered Denmark’s largest Viking Age silver hoard, which contained about 6.5 kilograms of silver.What does the silver hoard reveal about Vikings’ wealthThe Rebild hoard is unusual because most of its weight comes from silver bars, jewellery and cut silver rather than coins. This suggests the silver was not simply collected as a group of attractive objects. Instead, much of it appears to have been organised according to weight. During the Viking Age, silver could be used as a means of payment and as a store of value. Pieces were often cut into smaller parts, divided or melted down. What mattered was largely the weight and purity of the silver.The unusually large number of silver bars in the Rebild discovery falls into particular weight groups. Parts of the bracelets and pieces of cut silver show similar patterns. This indicates that the silver may have been deliberately organised as a substantial store of value rather than being randomly accumulated.What do the Viking coins reveal about the hoardThe hoard contains both Arabic and Anglo-Saxon coins, offering clues about the extensive connections of Viking Age Denmark. Among the findings, there are two Anglo-Saxon silver pennies minted during the reign of King Edward the Elder, who ruled from 899 to 924. These coins provide an important dating point because the hoard could not have been buried before such coins had entered circulation. The discovery also contains Arabic silver coins known as dirhams with inscriptions that can often be connected to particular mints and periods.Why is Rebild important for Viking Age discoveriesThe new silver hoard is not the only major Viking Age discovery from the Rebild area. In 1971, another large silver hoard known as the Rebild hoard was found nearby. It also dates to the 9th century and contained silver bars, jewellery and smaller pieces of silver. Altogether, it weighed around four kilograms and had been wrapped in animal skin when it was buried. Another recent discovery from the wider area is the Rold hoard, consisting of six intact Viking Age gold arm rings weighing a combined 762.5 grams.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: TN assembly passes resolution urging Centre to make Tamil primary language of Madras high court
articles.summary: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the Centre to take steps to make Tamil the primary language of pro.
articles.body: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the Centre to take steps to make Tamil the primary language of proceedings, judgments, decrees and orders in the Madras high court.Chief minister C Joseph Vijay moved the resolution after question hour and said the state sought the necessary legal action under Article 348(2) of the Constitution and Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, to enable the use of Tamil in the high court.The resolution noted that Tamil had been the official language of Tamil Nadu under the Tamil Nadu Official Language Act, 1956. Sections 4-A and 4-B of the Act provided for the use of Tamil in recording evidence and issuing judgments, decrees and orders in subordinate courts, tribunals and other courts functioning under the high court.The assembly recalled that it had unanimously passed a resolution on Dec 6, 2006, seeking the use of Tamil in the Madras high court and forwarded it to the Centre. The Union law minister informed the Rajya Sabha in 2018 that the proposal had been referred to the Chief Justice of India and that the Supreme Court’s full court had not accepted it.The latest resolution said advances in legal Tamil, translation services, digital courts, legal databases and artificial intelligence had strengthened the case for reconsidering the proposal. It called for procedures to allow petitions, documents and arguments in Tamil and for judgments and court orders to be issued in Tamil.It also sought training in legal Tamil and translation for judges, lawyers and court staff.Members from the DMK, AIADMK, PMK, CPI, CPM, BJP and DMDK supported the resolution. articles.title: Why personal-guarantor recoveries are so tiny — and why Chandra’s was tinier still
articles.summary: India News: Subhash Chandra’s proposed repayment of a little over Rs 6 crore against more than Rs 22,000 crore of admitted claims worked out to less than 0.03%.Th.
articles.body: Subhash Chandra’s proposed repayment of a little over Rs 6 crore against more than Rs 22,000 crore of admitted claims worked out to less than 0.03%.That looks exceptionally small. And it was. But personal-guarantor insolvency cases have produced very low recoveries more generally.Data from the insolvency regulator shows that nearly 5,200 applications have been filed against personal guarantors since the process came into force in 2019-20. Only around 64 have so far ended in repayment plans approved by creditors and the tribunal. Across those cases, lenders recovered a little under Rs 235 crore — roughly 1% of their admitted claims.So the larger problem is not specific to Chandra — on September 1, a specially constituted five-member bench of the NCLT stayed the order approving it anyway — but that the amount a person guarantees can be very different from what is actually available by the time lenders try to collect.A personal guarantee creates a liability. It does not, by itself, preserve the wealth behind that liability.When lenders take a guarantee, they can look at the guarantor’s assets, liabilities, credit history and other guarantees already given. But unless specific property is separately pledged or mortgaged, those assets are not locked away for the lender.But years can pass between a loan being made and a guarantee being invoked. In the meantime, assets can fall in value, be sold, be pledged elsewhere or be used to meet other liabilities.Chandra’s case shows how large that gap can become. Net-worth certificates submitted to banks in 2017 and 2018 put his worth at more than Rs 40,000 crore. During the insolvency proceedings, he said his assets were worth a little under Rs 32 crore, most of them already mortgaged, leaving around Rs 6.5 crore.(Chandra has disputed the earlier figure, saying it did not represent what he personally owned.)If the problem is that the wealth behind the guarantee can disappear or become unavailable, one way to make guarantees more useful is to make sure some of that wealth remains in place.Lenders can, for instance, require a guarantor to maintain a minimum net worth or a minimum amount of liquid assets while the loan is outstanding. Such covenants are used elsewhere. One US guarantee filed with the securities regulator required the guarantors to maintain at least $90 million in net worth and $8 million in liquid assets, and restricted transfers that would take them below those levels.Another option is to back the guarantee with a specific asset. A house, for instance, can be mortgaged against the guarantee. India already allows this, and such arrangements give lenders something more concrete than a general promise backed by whatever assets happen to remain later.There is also the question of finding those assets once insolvency begins. Rules introduced in 2026 widened the disclosures that can be sought from personal guarantors to include assets held through nominees, trusts and companies, as well as assets they control or benefit from without formally owning them. Another rule allows certain undervalued transactions intended to put assets beyond creditors’ reach to be reversed.None of these measures can ensure full recovery. A guarantor can still genuinely lose wealth.But they can narrow the gap between what a guarantee appears to be worth when a loan is made and what lenders find when they finally try to enforce it.Get the full storyhere on TOI+Why did the government drag personal guarantors into insolvency at all? Not just to recover more — but to make corporate borrowing harder to shrug offDoes it work? A personal guarantor was once facing claims of over Rs 330 crore. She offered … Rs 1 lakhHow much can a personal guarantee really expose you to? In law, potentially the whole unpaid debtGet the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Berlin pledges €250 million for repairs to Ukraine's energy facilities
articles.summary: Germany is contributing a further €250 million ($290 million) towards the costs of urgent repair work on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. The Economy Ministr...
articles.body:
Germany pledges €250 million for urgent repair work on Ukraine's energy infrastructure to ensure energy and heating supply despite Russian attacks.

German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche emphasizes the importance of supporting Ukraine in protecting and rebuilding its energy infrastructure, with collaboration from the German business community.

Russia's repeated bombings of Ukraine's power stations and energy grids have led to a significant need for international aid, with Germany being the largest contributor to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund.

Germany is contributing a further €250 million ($290 million) towards the costs of urgent repair work on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

The Economy Ministry said on Thursday that the aid is intended to safeguard the supply of energy and heating to the Ukrainian population despite ongoing Russian attacks.

"The energy supply, in particular, remains a front line in this war. That is why we are supporting Ukraine in protecting and rebuilding its energy infrastructure and are calling on all international partners to make further efforts," said Economy Minister Katherina Reiche.

Support for Ukraine is being provided in collaboration with the German business community, she explained. "Thanks to their donations of energy supplies, 1.4 million people have already had their energy supply restored. At the same time, we are mobilizing private investment for the reconstruction."

Russia has repeatedly bombed Ukraine's power stations and energy grids. Last winter, millions of people in the capital, Kiev, were without heating and had barely any electricity for weeks.

According to the ministry, the Ukraine Energy Support Fund has raised around €2.4 billion from international donors since the war began four and a half years ago.

With a contribution of €810 million to date, Germany is the fund's largest contributor, with aid channelled through the KfW development bank.

articles.title: ‘BJP goons’ looted TMC office with police in confidence, claims Mamata; warns of protests in Delhi
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) supremo Mamata Banerjee on Thursday accused BJP-backed men of vandalising her party's Camac Street office in Kolka.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) supremo Mamata Banerjee on Thursday accused BJP-backed men of vandalising her party's Camac Street office in Kolkata, alleging that documents and equipment were taken during the incident. The former West Bengal chief minister also alleged that the attackers acted with the "confidence" of the Kolkata Police.“We condemn the vandalism at our party office early in the morning in Kolkata. If this is the law and order situation in Kolkata, just imagine what is prevailing in rural areas,” Banerjee said during a Facebook Live.Alleging police involvement, Banerjee said, “BJP goons looted our documents and equipment and vandalised our office by taking Kolkata Police in confidence.”The former three-term chief minister also accused the BJP of indulging in "total lawlessness" in West Bengal and alleged that BJP workers were responsible for incidents at Jadavpur University.“What happened at Jadavpur University was the hooliganism of the BJP. We condemn this,” she said.Banerjee further alleged that an atmosphere was being created to restrict her movement, saying, “The chief minister is stating that they will not allow me to go out of my home.”She warned that the TMC would respond with demonstrations in the national capital if such 'atrocities' on the party continued.“If these atrocities on the TMC don't stop, we will stage dharnas outside BJP leaders' homes in New Delhi,” Banerjee said.Her remarks came hours after TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that armed, BJP-backed men vandalised the Camac Street office. He shared purported CCTV footage showing masked and helmeted men leaving the premises with electronic equipment, including television sets and a printer. Police subsequently arrested six people in connection with the incident, an officer said, according to PTI.Earlier on Thursday, the TMC had sought urgent meetings with president Droupadi Murmu and governor R N Ravi, alleging "utter lawlessness" and misuse of police by the BJP government. TMC Rajya Sabha leader Derek O'Brien said the party had written to both constitutional authorities.“For four months, this has gone from bad to worse. TMC workers are being targeted by the police across the state, party offices are being vandalised, police are following no rules, police are acting as openly as BJP cadres. There is utter lawlessness here,” O'Brien had alleged, according to PTI.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: After Google and Apple Maps change 'Lake Ontario' name to 'Lake America' for US users; one Map app has refused to follow what Trump calls 'ratified, binding' rule
articles.summary: Tech News News: Google Maps and Apple Maps followed federal directives to rebrand Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for users across the US but one app stood out for ‘no.
articles.body: Google Maps and Apple Maps followed federal directives to rebrand Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for users across the US but one app stood out for ‘not yielding’ – pushing it to No. 1 overall ranking on the US App Store, jumping up from the eighth position just a day earlier. The veteran digital navigation platform MapQuest drew a firm line in the sand, helping it return to prominence.The sudden surge in installations follows an August 27 executive order by President Donald Trump. While both Apple and Google quickly updated their platforms to reflect the change, MapQuest posted an announcement on X declaring that it would not comply with the rename. The company posted three different posts on the same:“We’re not changing it”, “We're not changing the name of Lake Ontario. Name it whatever you want at your leisure”, and “We are aware that Lake Ontario is being correctly labeled on our map.”The public pushback immediately resonated with mobile users looking for an alternative to Big Tech platforms. MapQuest sat at No. 128 on the US App Store on August 28 before jumping to No. 92 on August 29. By Monday, August 31, the platform surged to No. 3 overall while seizing the No. 1 rank in the Navigation category. By Tuesday (September 1), it sat on the top of the chart, holding the top spot across all applications and mobile games nationwide.Record downloads and active user engagementEstimates from analytics provider Sensor Tower show the app gained roughly 632,000 US downloads in the days following the presidential directive. In a direct statement, MapQuest stated total adoption was even higher, topping 1.5 million downloads across Canada and the US combined.“What’s been incredible is that people aren’t just installing our app — they care enough to communicate directly with us — making feature requests and submitting bug reports on social, and in our app reviews. Our small team has been working around the clock to build features people are asking for. We are aiming for everyone to have a great experience with the app,” MapQuest GM Doug Berger told TechCrunch.In the latest post on X, the app MapQuest said, “The people have spoken. We are working” and “MapQuest Engineers working overnight to release Android Auto ASAP”Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Tim Cook shares the letters that he has been reading every single day since past 15 years: Every morning ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: After a 15-year run as Apple’s CEO, Tim Cook has handed leadership to longtime insider John Ternus, moving into the role of executive chairman. Reflec.
articles.body: After a 15-year run as Apple’s CEO, Tim Cook has handed leadership to longtime insider John Ternus, moving into the role of executive chairman. Reflecting on his tenure, Cook shared one daily ritual that shaped his leadership and kept him connected to Apple’s users. As he reflects on his tenure at the helm of the $4.75 trillion tech giant, Cook has revealed one daily habit he credits with keeping him grounded throughout his run: reading customer emails, every single morning, without fail.A 15-year morning ritual of Tim CookCook revealed in a community letter that since 2011, he has begun nearly every morning by reading emails from Apple customers. “For the past 15 years I’ve started just about every morning the same way. I open my email and I read notes I received the day before from Apple’s users all over the world,” he wrote.These messages ranged from heartfelt stories about Apple products saving lives or capturing memories, to complaints about devices. Cook said it was an “honor and a privilege” to lead a company building transformative technology, adding: “In every one of those emails I feel the beating heart of our shared humanity… I feel a gratitude that I cannot put into words.”Tim Cook’s 4 am routineCook’s habit was part of a strict routine. He rises before 4 a.m., spends an hour reading hundreds of emails, then works out before diving back into customer feedback. He said the practice kept his “hands on the pulse of what customers are feeling and thinking and doing,” even as Apple navigated challenges like the pandemic, supply-chain disruptions, and the rise of AI.Read former Apple CEO Tim Cook’s complete letter hereTo the Apple community:For the past 15 years I’ve started just about every morning the same way. I open my email and I read notes I received the day before from Apple’s users all over the world.You share little pieces of your lives with me and tell me things you want me to know about how Apple has touched you. About the moment your mom was saved by her Apple Watch. About the perfect selfie you captured at the summit of a mountain that seemed impossible to climb. You thank me for the ways Mac has changed what you can do at work and sometimes give me a hard time because something you care about isn’t working like it should.In every one of those emails I feel the beating heart of our shared humanity. I feel a sense of deepening obligation to work harder and push further. But most of all, I feel a gratitude that I cannot put into words, that I somehow got to be the person on the other end of those emails, the leader of a company that ignites imaginations and enriches lives in such profound ways it defies description. What an honor and a privilege it has been.Today we announced that I’m taking the next step in my journey at Apple. Over the coming months I will be transitioning into a new role, leaving the CEO job behind in September and becoming Apple’s executive chairman. A new person will be stepping into what I know in my heart is the best job in the world. That leader is John Ternus, a brilliant engineer and thinker who has spent the past 25 years building the Apple products our users love so much, obsessed with every detail, focused on every possible way we can make something better, bolder, more beautiful, and more meaningful. He is the perfect person for the job.John cares so much about who we are at Apple, what we do at Apple, who we reach at Apple, and he has the heart and character to lead with extraordinary integrity. I am so proud to call him Apple’s next CEO. This company will reach such incredible heights under his leadership, and you will feel his impact in every bit of delight and discovery that grows out of the products and services to come. I can’t wait for you to get to know him like I do.This is not goodbye. But at this moment of transition, I wanted to take the opportunity to say thank you. Not on behalf of the company, this time, though there is a wellspring of gratitude for you that overflows inside our walls. But simply on behalf of me. Tim. A person who grew up in a rural place in a different time and, for these magical moments, got to be the CEO of the greatest company in the world. Thank you for the confidence and kindness you’ve shown me. Thank you for saying hi to me on the street and in our stores. Thank you for cheering alongside me when we unveiled a new product or service. Thank you, most of all, for believing in me to lead the company that has always put you at the center of our work. Every day we get up and think about what we can do to make your life a little bit better. And every day, you’ve made mine the best I could have asked for.Thank you.Tim Cook Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Embattled Spanish PM insists no prior warnings before Ceuta crisis
articles.summary: Spain's prime minister tells parliament it is absurd to think the government knew and did nothing, after thousands join protests in Spanish cities.
articles.body:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said no-one foresaw the influx of 72,000 migrants in the exclave of Ceuta, as pressure mounts over his handling of the crisis.

"It's absurd to think that the government knew and did nothing," Sánchez told Spain's parliament on Thursday, hours after tens of thousands of people joined protests across the country backed by opposition parties.

Sánchez also maintained there was no evidence Morocco was behind the mass crossing and there had been "close co-ordination" between the two countries.

A Spanish police report has highlighted the "total permissiveness" of Moroccan security forces, although senior officials insist it does not point the finger at Rabat.

Although most of the migrants have been sent back to Morocco, some 5,000 remain on the streets and beaches of Ceuta, on the North African coast, including as many as 1,400 children.

There have been several reports that Spanish officials had been warned of a rise in sea arrivals over the border at Ceuta, following a Spanish court ruling that many migrants misunderstood to mean they would not be pushed back if they swam across.

Opposition People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo accused the government of lying and a cover-up, and said the prime minister should resign.

Spain's handling of the migrant influx angered some of its European partners, and Italy responded by imposing border restrictions on arrivals from Spain.

The large turnout for the demonstrations in Madrid and other cities on Wednesday underlined the pressure Sánchez is under domestically too.

The protests were ostensibly held to express support for the people of Ceuta, but as frequent anti-government chants have shown, they also reflected public anger at the ongoing crisis.

As Thursday's fierce debate in Congress showed, the situation in Ceuta has developed from a humanitarian and logistical crisis into a major political challenge for the Socialist leader.

One of the issues Sánchez is having to explain is his government's bilateral relationship with Morocco.

He has tried to walk a delicate line between defending his refusal to blame Morocco while reprimanding it for the sovereignty claims it has been making in recent weeks on both Ceuta and its fellow Spanish exclave of Melilla.

Sánchez has been careful until now not to criticise Rabat and he said he would stick to "proven, verified facts", although he did complain of "unacceptable" statements by two Moroccan ministers about Ceuta and its sister city Melilla.

Moroccan Justice Minister Abdellatif Ouahbi has spoken of his country's "historical and geographical right" to the cities and proposed talks with Spain on the issue.

The two cities have the EU's only land borders in North Africa and Sánchez told parliament: "Ceuta is not the border of Spain, it is Spain on the border [of Europe]."

Politicians to both his left and right point to what they say is Morocco's track record of using the border with Spain as leverage when it has a grievance.

Many have interpreted the police report pointing to the role of Moroccan security forces in the July crossing as reinforcing this theory, although Sánchez maintained there was no solid evidence of government involvement.

The report, commissioned by a High Court judge, said security forces had "made no serious attempt" to stop the influx and quoted some migrants saying Moroccan gendarmes had even provided guidance.

Responding to the revelations, as well as media reports before the influx, Feijóo told MPs that the crisis had "originated in Morocco, was consented to by Morocco and there are indications that Morocco co-ordinated it and the government knew because it had been warned about it".

Morocco has denied orchestrating or being involved in the mass crossing.

Sánchez said King Felipe VI would visit Ceuta and Melilla in the coming weeks to convey Spain's commitment to the two cities, although officials say no date has been set.

He praised the response of Ceuta police who had chosen to "defend human life" when the influx took place, rather than defend the border. He also highlighted close co-operation with Moroccan authorities over the return of more than 90% of the migrants in the following 72 hours.

He addressed the "difficult times" faced by the residents of Ceuta, as he explained the "complexity" of what had happened on 30 and 31 July.

He spoke of an "episode in which numerous actors and interests converge", doubling down on his assertion that hoaxes and rumours spread by social media had sparked the crisis.

He has already blamed trafficking gangs and angered Russia and Israel for highlighting social media linked to both countries along with "an international far-right movement". He told MPs that there was no evidence of state actors being involved but doubled down on his allegations of accounts linked to the two countries.

Ceuta was "a humanitarian crisis and also an administrative challenge within the city itself", he added.

articles.title: Meet Gage Klein, the 16-year-old Pennsylvania student who has already opened his second restaurant while still in high school
articles.summary: US News: Gage Klein was taking orders, cooking food and working the register at his West York restaurant on a recent afternoon. The catch- he is only 16 and is.
articles.body: Gage Klein was taking orders, cooking food and working the register at his West York restaurant on a recent afternoon. The catch- he is only 16 and is already running his second restaurant while attending high school.According to AOL, Driftwood at the Fairgrounds in West York located at 1277 W. Market St., serves burgers, cheesesteaks, subs, hand-cut fries, wings and other items. The West York restaurant is Klein's second Driftwood location. His first, Driftwood at the Lake, opened more than a year ago in the Lake Meade community in Adams County. Both restaurants are part of a business built by the Klein family.Klein, who lives in West Manchester Township, said he and his father, Kris, wanted to expand beyond the Lake Meade community and reach more customers. They considered several possible locations, including places in Hanover and East Berlin, before finding a small restaurant space in West York. The site had previously been home to Steak Out.Interest in cooking started at homeKlein's interest in food began well before he started running restaurants. He said he has always had a passion for cooking, and his interest grew through spending time in the kitchen with his mother, Stacey.She would often prepare pasta for dinner. One day, Klein asked if he could make the sauce himself. His mother agreed, and after tasting it, she told him it was better than hers.That experience led the two to prepare more meals together. Over time, Klein began making a wider variety of dishes, including deviled eggs, boneless wings and traditional fettuccine Alfredo.One of the dishes he is particularly proud of came from an idea he had while he was bored. Klein created a grilled cheese pizza, topped with pieces of a grilled cheese sandwich.The unusual pizza is served at the Lake Meade restaurant during winter, when tomato soup is also on the menu. So far, only one customer has ordered the speciality pizza. But that customer gave it a positive review, calling it "a great pizza."Klein plans to attend culinary school after graduating from high school because he believes he still has a lot to learn about cooking.He has also expressed an interest in travelling to countries including Italy and Germany so he can experience food prepared in its country of origin.Balancing school and restaurantsKlein will be a junior at Commonwealth Charter Academy this year. Running two restaurants while attending school means he cannot spend all his time at the eateries.The restaurants have other employees who help operate them, particularly during the school year. Klein said some of his friends also visit the restaurants as customers.His work schedule can sometimes affect his free time. Some of his friends are disappointed when Klein does not have enough time to play video games with them because he is busy working.Despite being a teenager, Klein remains closely involved in the restaurants. A recent afternoon at the West York location showed him handling different parts of the business himself, from taking orders to cooking food and operating the register.Growing the family businessKris with his father created one of the restaurant's specialities, called The Driftwood Stack. The burger is made with two smash patties, four slices of American cheese, two slices of bacon, three onion rings, pickles, lettuce and tomato. It is finished with a secret sauce.Kris Klein said the restaurant has been receiving favourable reviews. Some customers are also travelling from southern York County to visit the West York location.The younger Klein wanted the menu to offer families better-quality food at a reasonable cost. That approach is reflected in the range of food available at the restaurant, including burgers, cheesesteaks, subs, wings and hand-cut fries.The hand-cut fries, covered with the restaurant's house seasoning, are among the popular side dishes. The wings are available in bone-in and boneless versions, with different sauces including classic Buffalo.Klein's role in the business is expected to grow further. At present, his father holds the majority ownership of the restaurant group so that he can sign legal documents for the business. That arrangement will change when Gage turns 18.For now, the teenager is already looking ahead. He has plans to continue opening more restaurants. His father believes his son stands out from other teenagers. "He's definitely a one of a kind kid," Kris Klein said, as quoted by AOL.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Himalaya death toll passes 1,270, with thousands still missing
articles.summary: The death toll in Nepal and Tibet has risen to 1,270, the authorities said, as thousands remain missing eight days after the devastating flooding in the Hima...
articles.body:
Severe flooding in Nepal and Tibet has resulted in a death toll of 1,270, with thousands still missing.

The flooding, linked to the collapse of glacial ice and rock in the Himalayas, caused extensive damage to homes, businesses, and structures in riverside communities.

Rescue efforts are ongoing, with many bodies recovered in Nepal remaining unidentified, while foreign nationals are among the missing individuals prompting international concern.

The death toll in Nepal and Tibet has risen to 1,270, the authorities said, as thousands remain missing eight days after the devastating flooding in the Himalayas.

In Nepal alone, 1,252 people have died, the police said, while in Tibet, the death toll rose from 16 to 21, the authorities said late on Wednesday evening.

In Nepal, 4,875 are missing, including 601 foreign nationals, according to official figures on Thursday.

In Tibet, 551 people are missing, the authorities said. There was no information about foreign nationals who may be unaccounted for.

Authorities abroad are seeking clarity about lost citizens. The German Foreign Office estimates that a high single-figure number of Germans are missing in both countries, it said in response to an enquiry.

Dozens of British nationals remain missing in Nepal, according to BBC reports.

Most of the bodies recovered so far in Nepal have not been identified. Authorities said rescuers were often finding only bone fragments or other human remains.

The flash floods swept away entire villages, causing billions of dollars worth of damage.

The flood is thought to have been triggered by the collapse of large quantities of glacial ice and rock in the Himalayas.

An access road to the badly affected border post at Gyirong in the Tibet Autonomous Region is now passable, enabling aid supplies to reach the disaster area more easily.
