articles.title: In 1953, a US Navy serviceman met his first love in Japan, but had to leave because war orders sent him home; nearly 70 years later, at 91, he finally found her again
articles.summary: US News: For nearly 70 years, an American man carried one question with him: Did Peggy Yamaguchi believe he had abandoned her? Duane Mann was 22 when he met Ya.
articles.body: For nearly 70 years, an American man carried one question with him: Did Peggy Yamaguchi believe he had abandoned her? Duane Mann was 22 when he met Yamaguchi in Japan in 1953. He was serving with the US Navy and she worked at a military club in Tokyo. They fell in love, planned to marry and were expecting a child. Then Mann received orders to return to the United States. He promised Peggy he would send for her. But once he reached home, the plan began to fall apart. His savings were gone, and the letters Peggy continued sending him never reached him.Mann eventually married twice and raised six children. Peggy married another man and built a family of her own. But Mann never stopped wondering whether she had spent her life believing that he had simply walked away.At 91, he decided to look for her. Nearly 70 years after they had last seen each other, Mann and Peggy reunited in Michigan on June 1, 2022.They met at a military club in TokyoAccording to KETV NewsWatch and accounts later shared by Mann, he was stationed in Japan in 1953 and was among seven Navy personnel based at Tokyo Haneda International Airport. His duties included handling priority Navy cargo. During his spare time, he worked as a slot-machine repairman at an Air Force non-commissioned officers' club. That was where he met Peggy, who worked in the club's hat-check room.The two began spending time together and dancing when they were off duty. Their relationship became serious and they decided to get married. Peggy became pregnant. But in June 1954, Mann was ordered back to the United States. He left Japan about a week later. Mann later recalled the departure in a Facebook post, saying he had left Peggy in tears and pregnant. He had reassured her that he had saved enough money to bring her to America. He believed they would soon be together again. He was wrong.Mann returned home but his savings were goneMann had left his bank account in his father's name while he was serving overseas, in case something happened to him. When he returned to Iowa in the US, he discovered that his father had spent the money. The savings he had planned to use to bring Peggy to the US were no longer there.Mann took a job with a highway construction company and began saving again. Meanwhile, he and Peggy continued writing to each other. Her letters were sent to Mann's family home. Then, from Mann's point of view, the correspondence suddenly stopped.He did not know that Peggy was still writing. According to KETV NewsWatch, Mann later learned that his mother had been burning Peggy's letters because she did not want her son to marry a Japanese woman. “She did not want me to marry a Japanese woman,” Mann told KETV NewsWatch.About three months after the letters stopped, Mann's younger sister gave him a final letter from Peggy. She had lost the baby and had married another man in 1955. For Mann, the discovery changed his understanding of what had happened. And one thought stayed with him: Peggy might have believed he had abandoned her.He married and raised six children but never forgot PeggyMann went on to marry twice and have six children. He built a life in Iowa, but Peggy remained part of his memories. As the years passed, he continued wondering what had become of her and whether she had blamed him for leaving. At 91, he decided to make one final attempt to find her. With help from his son Brian, Mann posted an old photograph of Peggy on Facebook and asked people to help locate her.The post eventually reached Theresa Wong, a Canadian researcher associated with the History Channel. According to KETV NewsWatch, Wong began looking through old records and found a 1956 newspaper article titled “Tokyo Bride likes life in Escanaba”.The article described a Japanese woman who had moved to Escanaba, Michigan, after marrying an American serviceman. It gave the search its crucial lead. Peggy was eventually located in Michigan. She was 91 too.Peggy had built a life in America tooPeggy had married in 1955 and moved to the US with her husband. She raised three sons. Yet Mann had not completely disappeared from her memories. One of her sons had the middle name Duane, the same as Mann's first name. After almost seven decades apart, the families arranged for the two to meet. On June 1, 2022, Mann travelled to Michigan with his son Brian. The reunion did not turn out to be awkward or distant. The two began talking about their time together in Japan and remembered dancing.Then Mann finally addressed the question that had troubled him for most of his adult life. “I was worried that you thought I abandoned you,” he told Peggy. “And I'm here to tell you that I didn't abandon you at all. I just couldn't find you.”Peggy reassured him. She also noticed that Mann had kept photographs of her for all those years. “You must have loved me,” she told him. “I did,” Mann replied.The reunion was not about starting overBy the time Mann and Peggy met again, both had lived separate lives, married and raised families. Their reunion was not about going back to the relationship they had as young people. For Mann, it was about finally explaining why he had never returned and finding out what Peggy had believed all those years. The reunion gave him the opportunity to tell her that directly.For Peggy, it also meant seeing the man she had loved in Japan after almost 70 years and discovering that he had not simply forgotten her. Mann later described the reunion as a freeing moment after carrying the story for so long.Mann has since died. But before his death, he was able to meet Peggy again and tell her the truth he had wanted her to know for nearly seven decades.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Kim Jong-un Era 2.0.’: North Korea drops reunification goal from party charter
articles.summary: Rest of World News: North Korea has formally removed its goal of reunification with South Korea from the charter of its ruling Workers’ Party of Korea, while expanding le.
articles.body: North Korea has formally removed its goal of reunification with South Korea from the charter of its ruling Workers’ Party of Korea, while expanding leader Kim Jong-un’s authority and further erasing references to the legacy of his predecessors.The revised charter, released in full for the first time on Thursday by South Korea’s Institute for National Security Strategy (INSS), provides the clearest documentary evidence yet of Pyongyang’s shift towards treating the two Koreas as “two hostile states.”The document removes references to “peaceful reunification of the country,” “united front,” “South Korea,” “great national unity” and pursuing political goals on a nationwide scale. It also deletes language calling for the withdrawal of US forces from South Korea and opposing foreign interference in the South.The changes reflect a policy shift announced by Kim in late 2023, when he declared that relations with Seoul were between two hostile states rather than two parts of a single nation. In January 2024, Kim called for constitutional provisions on peaceful reunification to be removed, with Pyongyang later confirming that the constitution had been amended.The revised party charter also strengthens Kim’s position within the ruling system. It removes the two remaining paragraphs describing the achievements and legacy of state founder Kim Il-sung and his successor Kim Jong-il, further shifting the party’s identity towards Kim Jong-un and his leadership.The charter now spells out the powers of the WPK general secretary in greater detail, including the authority to convene party meetings, appoint and dismiss officials, expel party members and dissolve party departments. The INSS said the changes reinforce Kim’s “unitary leadership system” as he approaches 15 years in power and enters what it calls the “Kim Jong-un Era 2.0.”The revised rules also allow the party to bypass internal election procedures during wartime and raise the minimum age for party membership from 18 to 20. The INSS said the change restores the original membership threshold introduced when the party was founded in 1945.One question remains unresolved: who currently holds the position of WPK first secretary, a post created in 2021 to act on behalf of the general secretary. North Korea has never publicly identified the officeholder, but the INSS assessed that senior party official Jo Yong-won is likely serving in the role.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: MrBeast reacts as viral Terraria kid reveals heartbreaking reason behind pause in Terraria videos
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A young Instagram creator known for sharing videos of himself playing Terraria has received support from MrBeast after sharing a sad update with his f.
articles.body: A young Instagram creator known for sharing videos of himself playing Terraria has received support from MrBeast after sharing a sad update with his followers. The creator, known online as michaelshowscoolthings, had been posting Terraria videos for more than a week. His simple videos, often filmed with a phone pointed at his screen, quickly became popular online. However, he recently said he needs to stop making the videos for a few days because his family is facing a difficult situation and preparing to move.MrBeast reacts after viral Terraria kid announces break from videosmichaelshowscoolthings told his followers that he would stop making Terraria videos for a short time because things in his personal life had become very difficult.“I’m gonna be stopping the Terraria videos for a little bit because everything has just been going horrible,” he said.The young creator explained that his family is moving, which means he cannot make his usual Terraria videos right now. He said he expects the break to last around four days.The creator later shared more about what was happening. He said he was “just really sad” about having to move. He also explained that his family is struggling with money and may have to move to a different state.He said his family is “so broke” that they have to move to another state. However, he added that his father wants to stay in their current state so he can try to start his own business.MrBeast shows support after Terraria creator shares emotional updateThe young creator’s update caught the attention of several people online, including one of YouTube’s biggest creators, MrBeast.MrBeast commented on the creator’s post with a short but supportive message, “Keep your head up.”The message came as the young creator was dealing with a major change in his life. MrBeast’s comment also helped bring more attention to the small creator, who had recently started going viral for his Terraria videos.Unlike many gaming creators who use powerful computers and recording software, michaelshowscoolthings has been filming his Terraria gameplay with a phone. This simple style has become part of what makes his videos stand out.His videos had been gaining attention on Instagram before he announced the short pause.For now, the creator says he plans to stop making Terraria videos for about four days while his family deals with the move and other problems. His followers will likely have to wait until things settle down before his regular videos return.MrBeast’s simple message gives the young creator some encouragement during a difficult time. While the break is expected to be short, the support from one of the world’s biggest YouTubers has given the viral Terraria creator plenty of reason to keep his head up.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
